question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed opt-in `gateway.readiness` contract, including required/advisory conditions, subject identity, and activation-scoped plugin providers, as a supported public direction?
rationale: This RFC introduces new user-visible configuration and plugin extension semantics. Automated review can assess consistency, but it cannot choose whether those contracts should exist or become durable OpenClaw API.

options.title: Accept and record the contract
options.body: Approve the opt-in readiness direction and record the accepted compatibility and plugin boundaries in the RFC or a linked maintainer discussion.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Limit the RFC to core readiness conditions and defer plugin providers or subject identity until maintainers choose those separate contracts.

options.title: Do not adopt this direction
options.body: Keep the legacy readiness model and decline the proposed public readiness framework.

recommendation.title: Accept and record the contract
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in readiness direction and record the accepted compatibility and plugin boundaries in the RFC or a linked maintainer discussion.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed participant in the supplied context with direct ownership of this RFC and its linked implementation stack.
